editorial.headline: Non-Edible Oilseed Farming That Bali Leaves Open to PMA
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers integrated farming and seed production for non-edible oil-bearing grains, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the slim record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01118 is a farming activity, but its focus is narrow and industrial rather than culinary. It covers oil-bearing grains that are not grown for cooking oil: cottonseed, flaxseed, mustard seed, niger seed, castor seed, and comparable non-edible oilseed crops named in the scope. The agricultural chain is also part of the definition. Land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work all sit within the activity when they are carried out as one integrated sequence. The same record also places nursery and seed-production activity for these non-edible oilseed plants inside the scope.

That matters because this is not merely a label for a crop. It is a registration home for operators whose business is the cultivation system around those crops, from seed or seedling activity through the field cycle and into post-harvest handling when those steps form one business line. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it is not reserved only for a single enterprise size. A small grower, a medium operator, or a larger agricultural company can all read the scale field as part of the same activity frame, provided the business remains within the stated non-edible oilseed scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is clean: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical editorial terms, that means the slim record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. The relevant source field is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and there is no separate number in the record that narrows the ceiling. The honest reading is therefore not a half-open category or a capped foreign stake; on the national data given here, this activity is open to foreign ownership up to the stated maximum.

The Bali picture is also unusually direct. The province-wide moratorium described in the record blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, but this activity is not marked as blocked. The reason given is specific: at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The national door and the Bali door are aligned here: the activity is foreign-open nationally, and the slim record does not put it inside Bali's PMA moratorium block. That does not add any permit, timeline, tax, or capital conclusion beyond the record; it simply means the Bali status field does not close the activity to PMA registration.
